questions.stem: Where and when is The Holdovers set?
options: At a Boston boarding school over the summer break of 1970
At a New England boarding school over Christmas 1970
At a New England boarding school over Thanksgiving 1970
At a New England boarding school over Christmas 1968
questions.explanation: The film is set at Barton Academy, a boarding school for boys in New England, over the Christmas break of 1970. The snowy, almost empty campus is where most of the story happens.

questions.stem: Why does the headmaster make Paul Hunham supervise the boys who stay at school over the break?
options: To punish him for failing a senator's son, who then lost his place at Princeton
Because Hunham volunteered, wanting quiet time on campus to write his monograph
Because the headmaster wants him to tutor the boys who failed his exam
To punish him for striking a student who had cheated in his ancient history exam
questions.explanation: Hunham refused to pass the son of a senator, and the boy's Princeton offer was withdrawn. Holdover duty is the headmaster's punishment, which shows how Barton bends to wealth and influence.

questions.stem: Why is Angus Tully stuck at Barton for the holidays?
options: His mother cancels their Christmas trip to go on a honeymoon with her new husband
He has been suspended and must sit his failed exams again before term starts
His father has forbidden him to come home after a fight over his poor grades
He chooses to stay so that he can finish an overdue essay on the history of ancient Rome
questions.explanation: At the last minute Angus's mother tells him she is spending Christmas on a honeymoon with his stepfather. Angus is left behind, which is the first sign of how alone he really is.

questions.stem: How do the other holdover boys leave Barton partway through the break?
options: They are sent home after Hunham reports them for breaking into the school kitchen at night
They run away to Boston together, leaving Angus behind because he refuses to go with them
A wealthy boy's father takes them skiing by helicopter, but Angus's parents can't be reached
Their parents drive up to collect them after the headmaster cancels the holdover program
questions.explanation: A rich student's father arrives in a helicopter and takes the boys on a ski trip. Angus needs his parents' permission, and Hunham cannot reach them, so only Angus, Hunham and Mary are left.

questions.stem: After Angus dislocates his shoulder running from Hunham in the gym, what does Angus do at the hospital?
options: He tells the doctor the truth, and Hunham is warned by the headmaster the next day
He invents a different accident and says it was his own fault, protecting Hunham
He tells the doctor that Hunham pushed him, hoping to have the teacher fired
He refuses to speak to the doctor until Hunham agrees to telephone his mother
questions.explanation: Angus could get Hunham into serious trouble, but he lies to the doctor to cover for him. It is a turning point: the two begin to trust each other.

questions.stem: At Lydia Crane's Christmas Eve party, what does Angus claim during an argument with Hunham?
options: That his mother is ill in hospital
That he has been expelled from Barton
That Mary is his real guardian
That his father is dead
questions.explanation: Angus says his father is dead, which is a lie the audience only understands later. In Boston it is revealed that his father is alive in a psychiatric hospital.

questions.stem: Who persuades Hunham to allow the trip to Boston?
options: Lydia, who offers to drive the three of them there
Danny, who wants to see a hockey game in the city
Woodrup, who telephones from his holiday to approve it
Mary, who gets a lift to visit her pregnant sister
questions.explanation: Mary convinces Hunham to take Angus to Boston, and she is dropped off in Roxbury to see her sister. Mary often sees what Angus needs more clearly than Hunham does.

questions.stem: In Boston, Hunham runs into an old Harvard classmate who has become a successful academic. What does Angus do?
options: He walks off in disgust and catches a taxi back to the school alone
He plays along with the false story Hunham tells about his own career
He tells the classmate the truth about Hunham's job at Barton Academy
He asks the classmate to help him find a place at Harvard after school
questions.explanation: Embarrassed, Hunham pretends to be a travelling scholar, and Angus backs him up. Angus now protects Hunham's pride, just as he protected his job at the hospital.

questions.stem: What does Hunham reveal about why he never finished at Harvard?
options: A rich classmate stole his work and blamed him, and Hunham hit him with his car
He failed his final exams after his father died and could not afford to repeat
He was caught copying another student's essay and was expelled for cheating
He left to fight in Korea and was never able to return to finish his degree
questions.explanation: A wealthy classmate plagiarised Hunham's work and framed him for it. Hunham hit him with a car, and was expelled. Like Angus, he was damaged by people with more privilege.

questions.stem: What is the real reason Angus wants to go to Boston?
options: To visit his father, who is alive in a psychiatric hospital
To meet his mother as she returns from her honeymoon trip
To sit an entrance exam for a different boarding school
To visit his father's grave, which he has never been allowed to see
questions.explanation: Angus slips away in a taxi, and Hunham follows, expecting a cemetery. Instead Angus visits his father, whose mental illness he fears he has inherited.

questions.stem: How does Hunham stop Angus from being sent to a military academy?
options: He tells the headmaster the visit to Angus's father was his idea, and is fired
He threatens to tell the board about the headmaster's treatment of the senator
He persuades Angus's stepfather that Angus has passed all his exams with honours
He offers to pay Angus's school fees himself if the boy is allowed to stay
questions.explanation: Angus's mother and stepfather want to move him to a military academy. Hunham takes the blame for the Boston visit, so Angus stays at Barton and Hunham loses his job.

questions.stem: How does the film end?
options: Hunham is given his job back after Angus admits the visit to his father was his own idea
Hunham and Mary leave Barton together to start a new life in the city of Boston
Angus leaves Barton with his mother while Hunham watches from the school's steps
Hunham drives away from Barton after tasting the headmaster's cognac and spitting it out
questions.explanation: Fired, Hunham takes the headmaster's expensive cognac, says goodbye to Angus, sips it in his car and spits it toward the school. He drives off, free of Barton.

questions.stem: Who is Mary Lamb?
options: The school's head cook, whose son Curtis was killed in Vietnam
The headmaster's assistant, who invites Hunham to her party
Angus's mother, who leaves him at school to go on her honeymoon
A nurse at the hospital where Angus's shoulder is treated
questions.explanation: Mary runs Barton's kitchen and stays over the break because it is her first Christmas since Curtis died. Her grief is one of the film's emotional centres.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes Paul Hunham at the start of the film?
options: A new teacher who is nervous about controlling a class of older boys
A rigid, unpopular classics teacher who holds every boy to harsh standards
A young, easygoing teacher who wants the boys to think of him as a friend
A famous historian who teaches at Barton to research his next big book
questions.explanation: Hunham teaches ancient history, is mocked by the boys and refuses to make exceptions for anyone. The film gradually shows the loneliness behind his strictness.

questions.stem: What does the film gradually reveal lies behind Angus's rudeness and defiance?
options: Boredom, because he finds the work at Barton far too easy for him
Envy of Teddy Kountze, who has taken his place as the best student
Loneliness, and a fear that he will become mentally ill like his father
Grief, because his father has died and his mother has quickly remarried
questions.explanation: Angus has been abandoned by his mother and has a father who is alive in a psychiatric hospital. At the hospital he admits he fears becoming like his father, which explains much of his behaviour.

questions.stem: Which parallel between Hunham and Angus does the film draw most clearly?
options: Both come from wealthy families who have always expected them to go on to Harvard
Both have lost a family member in the Vietnam War during the last year
Both plan to leave Barton for good as soon as the Christmas break is over
Both have been let down by more powerful people and are lonelier than they admit
questions.explanation: Hunham was framed at Harvard, and Angus has been left behind by his family. As each learns the other's secret, they recognise their shared isolation, and their relationship changes.

questions.stem: What does Mary give Hunham before he leaves Barton, and why does it matter?
options: A train ticket home, so he can see in the new year with his family
A letter for the headmaster, asking the school to give him his job back
A notebook, so he can finally begin the monograph he has always put off
Curtis's watch, to thank him for looking after Angus over Christmas
questions.explanation: Hunham once told Mary he wanted to write a monograph about Carthage but doubted he had a whole book in him. Her gift suggests that losing his job may free him to start.

questions.stem: Which war is going on in the background of the film?
options: The Korean War
The Second World War
The Gulf War
The Vietnam War
questions.explanation: In 1970 the United States was still fighting in Vietnam, and young men could be drafted. Mary's son Curtis has been killed there.

questions.stem: Mary could not afford to send Curtis to college. Why does this matter to his death?
options: Without college he could not train as an officer, so he was sent straight to the front
Without college he had no student deferment, so he could be drafted to Vietnam
Without college he could not get a job, so he volunteered for the army's pay
Without college he was not allowed to vote against the war in Vietnam
questions.explanation: In 1970, college students could defer being drafted. Curtis had the grades for college but not the money, so he was drafted, while Barton's rich boys were protected.

questions.stem: What does the film suggest through the contrast between Curtis and the Barton boys?
options: That in 1970 the burden of the war fell hardest on young men without money
That boarding schools in 1970 trained their students to become army officers
That the Barton boys were more patriotic than young men from poorer families
That the draft in 1970 chose young men fairly, whatever their background
questions.explanation: Curtis was a Barton student because his mother worked there, but he could not afford college. Rich boys could defer the draft; he could not. The film uses his death to expose class privilege.

questions.stem: How does Payne make The Holdovers feel like a film made in the early 1970s?
options: Period-style studio logos, film grain and colour, though it was shot digitally
It was shot on film stock left over from the 1970s and never digitally edited
It was filmed in black and white, like most American films of the time
It recreates the period through costumes and sets alone, with no visual effects
questions.explanation: The film was shot on a digital camera, then given grain, warm colour and retro logos to look like a film from 1970. The look, not just the costumes and sets, makes it feel like a film of its own period.

questions.stem: Which theme is most central to The Holdovers?
options: Lonely people forming an unlikely family and finding comfort in each other
The value of strict discipline in shaping boys into honourable young men
Young people rebelling against the authority of their elders around 1970
The healing power of going home to be with family at Christmas time
questions.explanation: Hunham, Angus and Mary have each been left behind, and over the break they become a kind of family. Strict discipline is what Hunham must learn to soften, and the film is about people who cannot go home. It suggests connection is possible even for people who have given up on it.

questions.stem: How does the film present grief?
options: As something Mary hides from the others, refusing to mention Curtis even at the Christmas party
As something shared openly with the whole school community at a memorial service for Curtis
As something carried quietly, as Mary keeps working through her first Christmas without Curtis
As something that passes quickly, once the characters return to their ordinary daily routines
questions.explanation: Mary keeps cooking and caring for others while mourning Curtis, and her grief breaks through at the Christmas Eve party. The film treats loss as something people live alongside.

questions.stem: The film's characters tell many lies. What makes Hunham's lie to the headmaster at the end different?
options: It is told to win back his job, rather than to help any other character
It is a lie that Angus asked him to tell, rather than one Hunham chose himself
It protects Angus at a real cost to himself, rather than protecting his own pride
It is told to the headmaster, a man Hunham respects, rather than to a stranger
questions.explanation: Hunham lied to his Harvard classmate to save face. At the end he chooses to lie to save Angus and loses his job, though he has no respect for the headmaster. The change shows how far he has moved toward caring for others.

questions.stem: How does the film explore privilege and integrity?
options: Hunham refuses to pass a senator's son and is punished, while Barton favours wealthy families
Hunham agrees to pass a senator's son and is rewarded, while the poorer boys are expelled
Hunham resents the rich boys because he was expelled from Harvard for his own cheating
Barton rewards Hunham's integrity, while the senator's son is made to repeat the year
questions.explanation: Barton rewards money and influence, and Hunham's honesty costs him twice: holdover duty, then his job. At Harvard he was framed by a richer classmate rather than caught cheating. Spitting out the headmaster's cognac is his final rejection of that system.

questions.stem: Hunham gives both Angus and Mary a copy of Marcus Aurelius's Meditations for Christmas. What does the gift suggest?
options: He thinks they need lessons in self-control after their angry outbursts
He is mocking them, knowing that neither of them enjoys reading
He reaches out to people through the classics, even if awkwardly
He wants to remind them that he is the most educated person there
questions.explanation: The gift is typical of Hunham: bookish, a little odd, but sincere. It shows him trying, in his own way, to connect with the people around him.

questions.stem: As he leaves, Hunham takes a bottle of the headmaster's very expensive cognac, sips it and spits it out. What does the cognac symbolise?
options: Mary's friendship, since she gave Hunham the bottle as a gift
The Christmas celebrations, which Hunham has always secretly loved
The wealth and privilege of Barton, which Hunham finally rejects
Hunham's drinking problem, which the film shows him overcoming
questions.explanation: The cognac was a gift to the headmaster from the trustees. Spitting it toward the school is a comic but pointed gesture: Hunham will no longer serve a place that serves money.

questions.stem: How does the soundtrack help to set the film in its period?
options: It uses punk and new wave songs to echo Angus's rebellious, angry mood
It uses songs from around 1970, by artists such as Cat Stevens, with Christmas songs
It uses mainly disco hits, the dance music that later ruled the 1970s radio
It relies on Mark Orton's original score alone, with no songs of the period
questions.explanation: Alongside Mark Orton's score, the film plays songs of the time by artists including Cat Stevens and Badfinger, and classic Christmas music. Disco and punk came later in the decade; these songs place the audience in 1970.

questions.stem: How does the setting of the snowbound, almost empty school shape the film?
options: It isolates the characters, forcing them together and stressing their loneliness
It creates a cheerful holiday mood, showing that Barton is a warm community
It provides danger, as the characters must survive a storm without help
It suggests peace and rest, giving the characters a holiday from their troubles
questions.explanation: With the other boys and staff gone, the empty halls and snowy grounds leave three people with only each other. The setting makes their loneliness visible rather than offering them rest.

questions.stem: Who says 'History is not simply the study of the past.'?
options: Angus, to his father, during his visit to the hospital
Hunham, to Angus, among ancient objects at a museum in Boston
Mary, to Hunham, while they watch television in the kitchen
The headmaster, to Hunham, when he gives him holdover duty
questions.explanation: In Boston, Hunham shows Angus ancient pottery and argues that the past helps explain the present. The line also fits Angus, whose present is shaped by his father's past.

questions.stem: At the museum, Hunham says, 'There's nothing new in human experience, Mr. Tully.' What idea does this express?
options: Human nature has changed, so history shows how far people have progressed
Each generation repeats the struggles of earlier ones, so the past can guide us
Modern life has made the lessons of ancient history useless to young people
Angus has had an easy life compared with the boys Hunham taught years ago
questions.explanation: Hunham argues that every generation thinks it invented suffering or rebellion, but people have always faced them. It is close to the film's own view: its 1970 story still speaks to audiences now.

questions.stem: Hunham tells Angus, 'You're not your father.' When does he say it, and what does it show?
options: After the hospital visit, reassuring Angus that he is not doomed to his father's illness
At the party, scolding Angus for lying to everyone there that his father was dead
At the school, defending Angus to his stepfather when he threatens to move him
On the first day, warning Angus not to expect special treatment because of his family
questions.explanation: Angus admits he fears he will end up like his father. Hunham's reassurance shows how much he has come to care for the boy.

questions.stem: Hunham tells Angus, 'I find the world a bitter and complicated place.' What does the line show?
options: Hunham mocking Angus for complaining about being left at school for Christmas
Hunham opening up, recognising that he and Angus share the same loneliness
Hunham warning Angus that he will fail his exam if he does not try harder
Hunham explaining to Angus why he hates spending the Christmas holidays with other people
questions.explanation: Hunham says this after Angus visits his father. He admits his own unhappiness and tells Angus they have it in common, a rare moment of honesty from a guarded man.

questions.stem: Hunham tells the headmaster, 'It was my idea,' about the visit to Angus's father. Why is this line a turning point?
options: It shows he wants to be fired so that he can return to Harvard
It reveals that he planned the visit before the holidays began
It is a lie that sacrifices his career to protect Angus's future
It is the first time he admits he took the boys to Boston at all
questions.explanation: The visit was Angus's plan, not Hunham's. By claiming it, Hunham keeps Angus at Barton and loses his job. The once rigid rule-keeper breaks a rule out of care.

questions.stem: Which is the strongest topic sentence for the prompt 'The Holdovers shows that people are changed by unexpected connections.' Discuss.
options: Payne suggests that Hunham's bond with Angus softens his rigid view of others
The Holdovers is a film by Alexander Payne that was released in the year 2023
This essay will discuss the connections between the characters in The Holdovers
Hunham is a classics teacher at Barton Academy who has to stay over Christmas
questions.explanation: A strong topic sentence takes a position on the prompt and names what the paragraph will prove. The others retell, announce or state facts without making an argument.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'Hunham spits out the cognac at the end.' How could this be turned into analysis?
options: Add a quotation from the scene where Hunham says goodbye to Angus
Retell what happens just before, when Hunham is fired by the headmaster
Explain how the gesture shows Hunham rejecting Barton's privilege as he leaves
Name the technique, a symbol, and say that it is a powerful one
questions.explanation: Analysis explains what the evidence suggests. Naming a technique, adding a quotation or retelling the plot does not do this; linking the gesture to the film's criticism of privilege turns a plot detail into an argument.
